angle: a cutaway of the object at work, so the inside explains it
subject: The heaviest bead on the glass with the drops it gathered pulled back off the pane along the line the rain came in on, each drop floating over the spot where it landed (its height is its note) with a hairline back to that spot and the slide it made down into the bead.
controls: rate: how many plain beads cling on the glass around the assembly (count), the drops that haven't gathered yet.
roof: how far apart the exploded drops' landing spots are in height (position, the parts fan from one line at 0 st to a tall spread at 36 st), so the span reads as the fan's height.
gust: the explosion axis tilts left or right (rotation of every leader, about ±30°), because the parts are pulled back along the direction the wind brought them in.
puddle: how many drops the heavy bead holds (count of exploded parts, 3 at 0 to 12 at 100, and the bead's size with them); each new drop enters on the right, bright, and the oldest leaves.
reference: exploded-view drawing convention (parts offset along one axis with leader lines); library/toro-blocks (one camera, hidden-line bodies)
risks: Leaders plus slide lines plus contact rings can read as a node graph or a molecule rather than drops; the leaders need to stay parallel and the slides quiet.
Floating flattened spheres risk reading as balloons on strings; they're drawn as real falling drops (pressed flat on the leading face), not as the teardrop icon.
The assembly only shows the puddle's memory; the beads around it are history and don't connect to it, so the screen has two stories.
Every note shifts all the parts one slot (n nodes move), so at puddle 100 a note moves 12 parts: peak cost grows with puddle.
Muted: the parts sink back to their contact rings (exploded distance eases to 0) and the bead goes G4: assembled and still.
